title: Foundations: Prog Metal - The Complete Guide
summary: What Prog Metal is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Prog Metal songs: Progressive metal applies prog-rock ambition to metal muscle: odd time signatures, concept albums, and conservatory-level musicianship. Dream Theater made 20-minute songs commercial.

History: Queensrÿche's Operation: Mindcrime (1988) and Dream Theater's Images and Words (1992) defined it; Tool, Opeth, and Mastodon pushed it into art-metal territory.

How the songs work: Prog Metal favors the keys of Em, Dm, Am, F#m. Common forms include Multi-section epics with recurring themes; Concept albums telling one story. Players should master odd meters: 7/8, 5/4, 13/16 first, then polyrhythms: drums in 4, guitars in 7. Seven-strings; capos irrelevant.

summary: An original Prog Metal study in Dm drilling polyrhythms: drums in 4, guitars in 7.
body:

title: Pull Me Under - Prog Metal Song Study
summary: Harmonic blueprint and playing guide for Pull Me Under by Dream Theater (1992).
body:
Pull Me Under — Dream Theater, 1992. The eight-minute single that broke prog-metal.

HARMONIC BLUEPRINT (study chart, key of Am):
A5 | A5 | A#5 | A5

This study chart uses the 'Djent vamp' progression, the Prog Metal workhorse, to map how songs like this move. Form: multi-section epics with recurring themes. Listen for clean/harsh vocal dynamics (opeth) — it is the fingerprint of the style.

TO PLAY IT: set your tempo to the Prog Metal pocket, voice the chords cleanly, and let clean/harsh vocal dynamics (opeth). Seven-strings; capos irrelevant. (Song facts: title/artist/year are documented public records; the chart is an original study arrangement.)
